title: AAHA-Accredited Hospital Locator
summary: Search by address and specialty for hospitals that voluntarily meet AAHA accreditation standards across patient care, safety, diagnostics, and practice operations.
useWhen: Use this when you need a new primary hospital, want a second option for a medically complex senior dog, or need to check whether a nearby hospital is AAHA accredited.

title: Find a Rehabilitation Professional
summary: Search rehabilitation professionals by name, practice, state, degree, or certification. The directory explains common rehabilitation credentials and clearly says owners must evaluate fit.
useWhen: Use this when your dog is slow to rise, recovering from surgery, losing strength, or needs a rehabilitation plan coordinated with a veterinarian.

title: Board-Certified Sports Medicine & Rehabilitation Search
organization: American College of Veterinary Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation
summary: Search veterinarians who completed specialty residency training and board certification in veterinary sports medicine and rehabilitation.
useWhen: Use this for complex arthritis, neurologic weakness, repeated injury, difficult post-operative recovery, or when a general rehabilitation plan is not improving function.

title: Certified Canine Rehabilitation Therapist Search
summary: Search graduates trained as Certified Canine Rehabilitation Therapists and related rehabilitation professionals; listings may include home, hospital, and stand-alone practices.
useWhen: Use this when you need a rehabilitation-certified professional and want to ask who evaluates the dog, who performs exercises, and how progress is measured.

title: Animal Hospice & Palliative Care Association
organization: International Association for Animal Hospice and Palliative Care
summary: Professional education, guidelines, and certification information for comfort-oriented veterinary hospice and palliative care.
useWhen: Use this to understand hospice credentials and the scope of comfort-oriented care before comparing local providers.

title: In-Home Hospice, Quality-of-Life and Euthanasia Search
summary: A national network offering in-home euthanasia, hospice in selected areas, telehospice, quality-of-life support, aftercare coordination, and pet-loss resources.
useWhen: Use this when travel is hard for your dog, the family wants to understand a home goodbye, or you need a quality-of-life conversation before deciding.

title: At-Home Euthanasia by ZIP Code
summary: Search by ZIP code or veterinarian for licensed veterinarians who provide at-home euthanasia, with availability, pricing, scheduling, and aftercare options shown during booking.
useWhen: Use this when your dog is stable enough for a planned home appointment and you want to compare local availability and what is included before the day arrives.

title: Pet Loss & Bereavement Service Directory
organization: Association for Pet Loss and Bereavement
summary: A searchable directory covering pet-loss counselors, veterinary social workers, doulas, chaplains, support groups, in-home euthanasia, hospitals, and aftercare services.
useWhen: Use this when the type of support is unclear or you need to compare local and online options across emotional, spiritual, and practical care.

title: No-Charge Pet Loss Chat and Video Groups
organization: Association for Pet Loss and Bereavement
summary: Scheduled online chat rooms and video support groups for people grieving a companion animal, with separate educational resources for anticipatory grief and euthanasia.
useWhen: Use this when you need a low-pressure first step, want to listen before speaking, or feel that people around you do not understand pet loss.

title: Pet Loss Support Hotline and Resource Center
organization: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine
coverage: United States by phone; resources available online
summary: A veterinary-student volunteer hotline trained with professional grief counselors, plus guidance on grief, children, euthanasia, memorials, and additional support groups.
useWhen: Use this when you need a compassionate listener or a credible place to understand what grief can feel like. It is not a mental-health crisis line.

title: Pet Loss Support Helpline
organization: Tufts Cummings School of Veterinary Medicine
summary: A nonjudgmental pet-loss helpline with scheduled evening staffing and voicemail, plus curated links to university hotlines and grief resources.
useWhen: Use this when evenings feel hardest and you want to talk with someone who understands companion-animal loss without entering therapy immediately.

title: Free Remote Pet Loss Support Group
organization: Michigan State University Veterinary Medical Center
summary: A no-charge remote group run by Veterinary Social Work Services, generally meeting twice monthly and open to people whose pet was not treated at MSU.
useWhen: Use this when you want a recurring group led from a veterinary social-work setting and can attend at a scheduled time.

title: Pet Loss, Decision and Quality-of-Life Support
organization: Colorado State University Argus Wellness and Support
summary: University-based support for treatment decisions, quality of life, family conversations, euthanasia, and grief, with a public resource page listing groups and counselors.
useWhen: Use this when the medical decision and the emotional weight are tangled together, especially if your dog is a CSU hospital patient or you need Colorado resources.

title: Honoring the Bond
organization: The Ohio State University Veterinary Medical Center
coverage: Ohio State Veterinary Medical Center clients
summary: Veterinary social-work support for difficult care decisions, quality of life, euthanasia, family conversations, behavioral-care burden, and grief resources.
useWhen: Use this if your dog is treated at Ohio State and the family needs a social worker alongside the medical team, or use its public guides to prepare questions.

title: Veterinary Social Work Support
organization: University of Tennessee Center for Veterinary Social Work
summary: A university center offering animal-related grief and bereavement support, including information on its pet-loss support group and help finding appropriate resources.
useWhen: Use this when you want support grounded in veterinary social work or need help understanding whether a group, counselor, or community resource fits.

title: Virtual Pet Loss Support Groups
summary: Free coach-led groups, specialty groups, one-to-one sessions, and courses covering pet loss, anticipatory grief, unexpected loss, and behavioral euthanasia.
useWhen: Use this when you want a group matched to the kind of loss, or when anticipatory grief starts before your dog has died.

title: Pet Cemetery & Crematory Member Directory
organization: International Association of Pet Cemeteries and Crematories
summary: Search current member facilities and review the association's standards and accreditation information for pet cemeteries, crematories, and aftercare providers.
useWhen: Use this before choosing aftercare so you can compare identity tracking, individual versus communal care, transport, return timing, and written pricing.

title: Licensed Online Veterinarian Marketplace
coverage: United States, Canada, United Kingdom and other markets
summary: Browse veterinarian profiles and availability for video or chat appointments. What can be diagnosed or prescribed depends on location, law, and the veterinarian-client-patient relationship.
useWhen: Use this for non-emergency questions, medication clarification, chronic-condition follow-up, or triage when travel is difficult. Do not use it to delay emergency care.

title: Board-Certified Veterinary Behaviorist Search
summary: Search AVMA-recognized board-certified veterinary behaviorists who can evaluate medical and behavioral causes and prescribe medication when appropriate.
useWhen: Use this for new aggression, severe anxiety, panic, compulsive behavior, or behavior change that may involve pain, cognitive decline, medication, or another medical cause.

title: Veterinary Specialist Search
summary: A public search for board-certified veterinary specialists, including internal medicine, cardiology, neurology, oncology, and nutrition.
useWhen: Use this when your senior dog's diagnosis spans multiple systems, a condition is progressing despite treatment, or your primary veterinarian recommends referral care.

title: Emergency and Specialty Hospital Locator
summary: Search BluePearl hospitals and review whether each location offers emergency care and specialties such as oncology, surgery, neurology, cardiology, or internal medicine.
useWhen: Use this to plan the nearest specialty or emergency option before a crisis, then call the location to confirm hours, services, and current intake status.

title: 24/7 Veterinary Emergency Group Locations
summary: Search 24/7 emergency hospitals by location and call the hospital directly to discuss an urgent symptom before arrival.
useWhen: Use this for breathing trouble, collapse, seizure, severe pain, toxin exposure, inability to urinate, or another sudden change that cannot wait for a routine visit.

title: Urgent Care Grants
summary: Small grants for eligible urgent veterinary situations when a funding gap prevents care; eligibility, timing, and required treatment plans are explained on the official site.
useWhen: Use this after a veterinarian has examined the dog and provided a diagnosis and treatment estimate, while continuing to discuss time-sensitive care directly with the clinic.

title: REACH Veterinary Care Assistance
summary: A charitable-care program that helps AVMF REACH-enrolled veterinarians provide immediate care to animals whose owners face financial hardship.
useWhen: Ask your veterinary team whether they participate or know a local charitable-care pathway; owners generally do not apply as if it were a guaranteed consumer grant.

title: Professional Pet Sitter Locator
summary: Search professional pet-sitting businesses by ZIP or postal code, then interview candidates about insurance, medication routines, mobility handling, and emergency plans.
useWhen: Use this when a senior dog needs reliable bathroom breaks, familiar routines, medication reminders, or caregiver respite at home.

title: End-of-Life Pet Photography Network
summary: A network focused on end-of-life pet photography and educational resources for families and photographers.
useWhen: Use this when time may be short and you want a photographer comfortable working quietly at home with a sick, anxious, or mobility-limited dog.

title: Animal Poison Control Center
summary: Veterinary toxicology guidance for suspected exposure to medications, foods, plants, chemicals, or household products. A consultation fee may apply.
useWhen: Call promptly with the product name, package, estimated amount, time of exposure, dog weight, and current symptoms; do not induce vomiting unless directed.

title: Pet Poison Helpline
coverage: United States, Canada and the Caribbean by phone
summary: A fee-based animal poison service staffed by veterinary toxicology professionals for medication, food, plant, chemical, and household exposures.
useWhen: Use this immediately after a suspected ingestion or exposure while preparing to follow instructions or travel to an emergency hospital.

title: Integrative Veterinarian Directory
summary: Search member veterinarians who list integrative or holistic services, then confirm licensing, training, evidence, medication interactions, and coordination with primary care.
useWhen: Use this when exploring acupuncture or other complementary support as part of a veterinary plan, especially when a senior dog takes several medications.

title: Fear Free Professional Directory
summary: Search certified veterinary and pet-care professionals who have completed Fear Free education; certification does not replace checking medical scope, licensing, or senior-care experience.
useWhen: Use this when clinic visits, handling, grooming, or home care trigger fear and you want to ask how the professional reduces stress for an older dog.

title: Animal Health Studies Database
coverage: United States and selected international studies
summary: Search recruiting veterinary clinical studies by species, condition, and location, then review eligibility, risks, costs, travel, and standard-care options with your veterinarian.
useWhen: Use this when a specialist mentions a study or when standard options are limited and the family wants to understand whether a legitimate university or hospital trial exists.

title: Pet Trust Planning Guide
summary: A practical overview of pet trusts and care planning, including choosing a caregiver, naming a trustee, leaving written instructions, and working with an attorney licensed in your state.
useWhen: Use this before a hospitalization, long trip, or family transition to create a written care plan and identify who can make decisions for your dog if you cannot.

title: Board-Certified Veterinary Nutritionist Search
organization: American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine
summary: Search the ACVIM directory specifically for board-certified veterinary nutrition specialists by country, state, city or ZIP code.
useWhen: Use this when a dog needs an individualized nutrition plan for weight change, chronic disease, food tolerance, or a complex home-prepared diet.
